subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should OpenClaw promote Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk to a first-class Gateway Relay path now, and should the first supported auth mode be API-key-only or wait for Microsoft Entra/managed identity support?
rationale: The remaining work changes provider routing and credential handling for browser-facing Talk, so automation should not choose the Azure auth/security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Ship API-key relay first
options.body: Implement the GA Azure Gateway Relay path with server-side API keys, SecretRef docs, Azure diagnostics, tests, and live proof, then track Entra/managed identity as a follow-up.

options.title: Require Entra before support
options.body: Delay first-class Azure Talk until Microsoft Entra or managed identity is designed and proven alongside API-key behavior.

options.title: Keep diagnostic-only for now
options.body: Leave Azure Realtime Talk unsupported beyond diagnostics until Azure quota/model availability and product demand justify the provider work.

recommendation.title: Ship API-key relay first
recommendation.body: Implement the GA Azure Gateway Relay path with server-side API keys, SecretRef docs, Azure diagnostics, tests, and live proof, then track Entra/managed identity as a follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal is the merged GA Realtime bridge work in the same OpenAI provider and Talk docs surface.
